security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel code on RISC-V accesses sireg* (or vsireg*) without first saving/restoring the corresponding siselect (or vsiselect) across context switches, or performs a non-atomic siselect-write + sireg-read sequence on a preemptible kernel path. Because siselect and sireg* form an indirect register window, a context switch or interrupt handler that modifies siselect between the two operations causes the kernel to read CSR state selected by a different execution context, violating the spec's implicit atomicity expectation for the select+access pair.
security_spec.summary: siselect/sireg* indirect CSR window is inherently TOCTOU-prone: a preemptible kernel path or missing context-switch save/restore of the selector register leaks CSR state between processes or VMs on the same hart

findings.finding: FreeBSD does not implement the Sscsrind/Smcsrind indirect CSR access extension. No CSR definitions exist for siselect (0x150), sireg* (0x151-0x157), vsiselect (0x250), vsireg* (0x251-0x257), miselect (0x350), or mireg* (0x351-0x357). The riscvreg.h header contains no macros for any indirect CSR access registers.
findings.snippet: N/A — no siselect/sireg/vsiselect/vsireg/miselect/mireg definitions exist in the file

spec_citations.excerpt: Supervisor-level CSRs: siselect (0x150), sireg (0x151), sireg2 (0x152), sireg3 (0x153), sireg4 (0x155), sireg5 (0x156), sireg6 (0x157). The CSRs in the table above are required if S-mode is implemented.

The value of miselect determines which register is accessed upon read or write of each of the machine indirect alias CSRs (mireg*). miselect value ranges are allocated to dependent extensions, which specify the register state accessible via each mireg_i register, for each miselect value.

findings.finding: The context switch routine does not save or restore siselect or any sireg* CSRs, because the Sscsrind extension is not currently supported. If this extension were implemented without corresponding context-switch support, a context switch between the siselect write and sireg read would cause CSR state to be read from the wrong execution context (info leak).
findings.snippet:
cpu_switch:
  sd a1, PC_CURTHREAD(tp)
  ld x13, TD_PCB(a1)
  sd x13, PC_CURPCB(tp)
  ld x13, TD_PCB(a0)
  sd ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
  ... // no siselect/sireg save/restore

findings.finding: The bhyve hypervisor (vmm) does not virtualize vsiselect or vsireg* CSRs for guest VMs, because the Sscsrind/Smcsrind extension is not currently supported. No vmm code references any indirect CSR access registers.
findings.snippet: N/A — no vsiselect/vsireg handling exists in the vmm subsystem

spec_citations.excerpt: A virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect or vsireg*, or attempts from VU-mode to access siselect or sireg*.
